claims.text: The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is in a solidified solid-solution state.
The temperature- and strain-rate-dependent dynamic behavior is governed by an interaction between dislocation glide and grain-boundary-mediated deformation.
The relative activity of dislocation glide and grain-boundary-mediated deformation is influenced by alloy composition and microstructure.
Higher temperatures produce lower strength relative to the room-temperature baseline.
Higher temperatures produce greater ductility relative to the room-temperature baseline.
Lower strain rates produce lower strength relative to the moderate-strain-rate baseline.
Lower strain rates produce greater ductility relative to the moderate-strain-rate baseline.
Lower temperatures produce greater strength relative to the room-temperature baseline.
Lower temperatures produce lower ductility relative to the room-temperature baseline.
Higher strain rates produce greater strength relative to the moderate-strain-rate baseline.
Higher strain rates produce lower ductility relative to the moderate-strain-rate baseline.
Outside an unspecified strength–ductility regime, behavior becomes dominated by brittle fracture or excessive deformation.
Room temperature and a moderate strain rate are designated as the comparison baseline.
